content.title: About
content.content: Cherries are the edible fruits of the sweet cherry tree (Prunus cerasus). Dark red, sweet, raw cherries have a bright aroma, juicy flesh and a mildly tart‑sweet flavor. They are eaten fresh and also used in baking, desserts, jams and beverages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherries belong to the same family as almonds, peaches, plums and sweet cherries.
Edible cherries contain small pits that are rich in antioxidants.
There are over 400 cherry varieties differing in taste, color and harvest time.
Cherries are often used in traditional medicine to aid digestion and reduce inflammation.
Cherry juice and compote are popular refreshing drinks in Eastern Europe.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cherries provide anthocyanins and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids in cherries promote better blood flow and may lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C enhances the body's defensive mechanisms.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cherries.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Large amounts of acidic cherries can irritate the stomach in people with high gastric acidity.

items.title: Pit safety
items.content: Cherry pits contain amygdalin, which can convert to cyanide if chewed; pits should be removed before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cherries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, oatmeal, salads, baked into pies, jams and compotes. For a softer texture they are sometimes soaked in cold water for 30 minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cherries in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze the berries in a single layer on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag.
